source_title: Tropicana Line's Sales Plunge 20% Post-Rebranding (Ad Age)
publisher_issuer: Ad Age (Advertising Age); this record is a second independent credible source corroborating slice-2 SRC-066
company_context: PepsiCo's Tropicana launched a redesigned Pure Premium package on January 8, 2009, replacing the iconic orange-and-straw imagery with a plain glass of juice and a restyled logo and cap, supported by an Arnell-created campaign. Ad Age reported the sales collapse and reversal, independently corroborating the figures in slice-2 SRC-066.
business_type: Consumer packaged goods - branded chilled orange juice; shelf-recognition-dependent purchase
macro_context: Recession-era CPG environment with private-label pressure in chilled juice; in-store brand recognition critical to repeat purchase.
evidence_summary: Ad Age independently corroborates the slice-2 SRC-066 figures: after the Pure Premium package redesign launched January 8, 2009, sales of the Tropicana Pure Premium line plummeted about 20% between January 1 and February 22, costing the brand tens of millions of dollars (about $30 million as reported elsewhere), and on February 23 PepsiCo announced it would scrap the new packaging and revert to the original. The redesign and supporting campaign by agency Arnell cost about $35 million. The precise dating (Jan 1-Feb 22 decline; Feb 23 reversal) strengthens the SRC-066 record beyond a single secondary blog.
owner_decision_context: Brand management approved a full redesign of an iconic, high-recognition package to modernize it, underweighting the shelf-recognition equity driving repeat purchase; the rapid reversal corrected the error within weeks.
action_taken: Launched the redesigned Pure Premium package on January 8, 2009 with a ~$35 million Arnell campaign; reversed on February 23, 2009 by reinstating the original packaging after sales fell about 20%.
outcome_evidence: An approximately 20% sales decline between January 1 and February 22, 2009 followed by a February 23 announcement to revert confirms the redesign action directly caused the drop and was corrected, corroborating SRC-066.
source_limitations: WebFetch of Ad Age returns HTTP 403 here; figures verified from search snippets quoting the Ad Age article (and consistent across Packaging Digest and Fortune) rather than full-text read. Ad Age is credible trade journalism, not an audited PepsiCo disclosure; the ~$30 million loss figure is an estimate, while the 20% decline and Jan 1-Feb 22 / Feb 23 dates are stated directly.
directly_stated: Sales of the Tropicana Pure Premium line plummeted about 20% between January 1 and February 22, 2009
On February 23, 2009 PepsiCo announced it would scrap the new packaging
The redesign campaign by agency Arnell cost about $35 million
inferred: Loss of shelf recognition was the mechanism of the decline (a go-to-market/shopper-identification failure)
The action was the proximate cause given the immediate decline and rapid reversal
why_useful_for_opsiq: corroboration for SRC-066: a second independent credible source (Ad Age) confirming the Tropicana 2009 redesign sales-drop figure (about 20%, Jan 1-Feb 22) and the Feb 23 reversal. Raises confidence in the slice-2 record (currently C-rated) and supports outcome-10 wrong-action-then-correction and gtm_channel_mismatch modeling.
